disclaimer: Legal mapping is indicative, not legal advice. Code scanning cannot see contracts, privacy policies or offline processes.

findings.title: Personal data exposed by an unauthenticated route
findings.evidence: GET /api/users/<int:user_id> (get_user) returns email, full_name, phone with no authentication check; anyone can change <int:user_id> to read other people's data (IDOR)

lines: "SELECT full_name, email, phone, city FROM users WHERE id = ?", (user_id,)

findings.severity_reason: Directly exploitable over the network by anyone.
findings.fix: Require authentication and check that the requester owns the record.

findings.title: Hardcoded secrets or credentials

law.requirement: Measures to control access to computer resources.

findings.severity_reason: Anyone with repo access can reach the systems that hold personal data.
findings.fix: Move secrets to a secret manager or environment, rotate exposed keys, add .env to .gitignore.

findings.title: Tracking or targeted ads possible for children
findings.evidence: <script async src="https://www.googletagmanager.com/gtag/js?id=G-LENDDEMO01"></script> [Google Analytics (gtag.js) runs for every user, children included: the app collects date of birth / age (the backend reads 'dob', app.py:90) but no age check stops the tracking]

lines: <!-- Analytics on the sign-up page, which asks for the date of birth -->

law.requirement: No tracking, behavioural monitoring or targeted advertising directed at children.

findings.severity_reason: Rs 200 crore cap and an outright prohibition.
findings.fix: Disable tracking and ad SDKs for users under 18.

findings.title: Insecure infrastructure configuration
findings.evidence: No USER instruction after 'FROM python:3.11-slim': the container runs as root

law.requirement: Access control and appropriate technical and organisational measures.

findings.severity_reason: Raises the chance and impact of a breach of stored personal data.
findings.fix: Run as non-root, disable debug in production, restrict CORS, enforce TLS, block public buckets.

findings.title: Weak password hashing
findings.evidence: return hashlib.md5(password.encode()).hexdigest() [md5: password hashed with a fast, unsalted hash]

law.requirement: Reasonable security safeguards to prevent personal data breach.

findings.severity_reason: Fast hashes are easily cracked after a leak.
findings.fix: Use bcrypt, scrypt or argon2 with per-user salt.

findings.title: Child data collected without parental consent flow
findings.evidence: Date of birth / age is collected (the backend reads 'dob'), but no parent or guardian consent flow exists anywhere, so under-18s are processed without a parent's consent

lines: return jsonify(error="consent to KYC processing is required"), 400
full_name, email, phone = form["full_name"], form["email"], form["phone"]
"INSERT INTO users (full_name, email, phone, dob, aadhaar, city, password_hash, created_at)"

law.requirement: Verifiable consent of the parent before processing a child's personal data.

findings.severity_reason: Rs 200 crore cap; affects a protected group.
findings.fix: Gate under-18 sign-ups behind verified parental consent (Rule 10 methods).

findings.title: Personal data written to logs
findings.evidence: log.info("New signup: %s, %s, aadhaar %s", email, phone, aadhaar)

lines: log.info("New signup: %s, %s, aadhaar %s", email, phone, aadhaar)

law.requirement: Secure personal data through encryption, obfuscation, masking or virtual tokens.

findings.severity_reason: Logs are widely accessible and long-lived; unmasked PII there is a common breach source.
findings.fix: Mask or tokenise PII before logging (e.g. a***@x.com, ******1234).

findings.title: Consent can be given but not withdrawn
findings.evidence: POST /consent (give_consent) grants consent; no route anywhere withdraws or revokes it

law.requirement: Withdrawal must be possible at any time, with ease comparable to giving consent; processing must then stop.

penalty.provision: any other provision of the Act or Rules

findings.severity_reason: Consent is the legal basis for processing; with no withdrawal path the user cannot stop it.
findings.fix: Add DELETE /consent (or POST /consent/withdraw) that clears consent and stops downstream processing.

findings.title: Excessive data in API responses
findings.evidence: return jsonify(dict(row)) [GET /api/kyc/<int:user_id> (kyc_record) sends SELECT * FROM users with aadhaar, password; return only the fields the client needs]

lines: row = db().execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?", (user_id,)).fetchone()
# --- Compliant look-alikes (answer key: ground_truth.yml, "compliant"). Nothing here may be reported.

law.requirement: Masking and minimising exposed personal data.

findings.severity_reason: Sensitive fields leak to every client, including logs and caches.
findings.fix: Return a response schema/serializer with only the needed fields; mask identifiers.

findings.title: Personal data stored in plaintext
findings.evidence: aadhaar TEXT NOT NULL, [users.aadhaar stored as TEXT]

law.requirement: Encryption, obfuscation, masking or virtual tokens.

findings.severity_reason: A database leak exposes the data directly.
findings.fix: Encrypt sensitive columns at the field level, or store tokens instead of raw values.

findings.title: Pre-ticked or default-true consent
findings.evidence: <input type="checkbox" name="marketing_consent" value="yes" checked> [consent checkbox is ticked by default]

lines: मैं KYC और अपने ऋण आवेदन के लिए अपने डेटा के प्रसंस्करण से सहमत हूँ।
Send me offers and product updates.
मुझे ऑफ़र और उत्पाद अपडेट भेजें।

law.requirement: Consent must be unambiguous with a clear affirmative action.

penalty.provision: any other provision of the Act or Rules

findings.severity_reason: A default 'yes' is not an affirmative action, so consent may be invalid for all users.
findings.fix: Default consent to false and require an explicit user action.

findings.title: Personal data sent to a third-party SDK
findings.evidence: mp.track(str(user_id), "Signed Up", {"$email": email, "$phone": phone, "city": city}) [email, phone sent to Mixpanel]

law.requirement: Fiduciary is responsible for processors, which must work under a valid contract with security terms.

penalty.provision: any other provision of the Act or Rules

findings.severity_reason: Data leaves your control; contract status cannot be verified from code.
findings.fix: Send pseudonymous IDs instead of PII, scrub events, and confirm a DPA exists with the vendor.

findings.title: Immediate hard delete with no minimum retention
findings.evidence: db().execute("DELETE FROM users WHERE id = ?", (user_id,)) [delete_account() hard-deletes users immediately; also wipes audit_log, consents at once]

law.requirement: Retain personal data, traffic data and processing logs for at least one year, then erase.

penalty.provision: any other provision of the Act or Rules

findings.severity_reason: Counter-intuitive gap: deleting too early also breaches the Rules.
findings.fix: Soft-delete and restrict access, keep processing logs for one year, then purge.
